_comment: Physical and Environmental Protection Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs with MA (PE-3 escort + maintenance overlap), MP (PE-16 delivery + removal echoes MP-5 transport), CP (PE-9/10/11/12/13/14 environmental safeguards underpin CP-2 contingency planning), and PS (PE-2 access authorization tracks personnel screening from PS-3). Often largely inherited when the system runs on FedRAMP-authorized cloud — the inheritance pattern is itself worth documenting clearly.
title: Physical and Environmental Protection Plan
description: Documents how the facilities, environmental systems, and physical-access controls protecting the system are governed. Covers physical-access authorization, physical-access control, transmission and output-device protection, monitoring and visitor logging, emergency systems (power, lighting, fire suppression, water leak detection, HVAC), environmental protection, secure delivery and removal of assets, and alternate work-site protection. Covers the controls of the PE family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NFPA 75 (Fire Protection of Information Technology Equipment), TIA-942 (Data Center Standards), Uptime Institute Tier ratings, NIST SP 800-46 r2 (Telework Security), and FedRAMP physical-control inheritance models.
intro_template:
This Physical and Environmental Protection Plan documents the physical and environmental safeguards applied to {system_name}'s hosting facilities. It establishes the practices, controls, cadences, and roles used to authorize and control physical access, monitor activity at facility boundaries, log visitors, sustain emergency power and lighting, suppress fire, detect water leaks, control temperature and humidity, manage secure delivery and removal of assets, and protect alternate work sites where telework is performed.

The scope covers physical access authorization, physical access control, transmission and output-device protection, monitoring and visitor logging, emergency power / lighting / fire / water / HVAC, secure delivery and removal, and alternate work-site protections within the {system_name} authorization boundary. Where controls are inherited from an underlying provider (FedRAMP IaaS, hosting facility), the inheritance posture and provider-supplied evidence are explicitly cited. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Physical and Environmental Protection family), NFPA 75 (Fire Protection of IT Equipment), and NIST SP 800-46 r2 (Telework Security).
approach_template:
{system_name} is hosted in {hosting_model}. The primary facility is {primary_facility}; the alternate / disaster-recovery facility is {alternate_facility}. Physical access is governed by {access_governance_role} via {access_request_workflow}. Visitor logging is performed at {visitor_logging_location}. Environmental protections — fire suppression, power, HVAC, water-leak detection — are inherited from {environmental_inheritance_provider} where the system runs on a managed facility, with provider-supplied evidence at {provider_evidence_location}.

Additional details on facility inventory, physical access authorization, physical access control, transmission and output protections, monitoring and visitor management, emergency systems, environmental protection, asset disposition, and alternate work-site protection are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Physical-and-environmental performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (badge-access denial rate, lost-badge incidents, environmental-alarm count by category, emergency-power test results, fire-suppression inspection currency, visitor-log completeness rate). The provider's continuous-monitoring posture is reviewed on the cadence in §6.2; for inherited controls, FedRAMP / SOC 2 audit reports are pulled annually to confirm provider control effectiveness. Environmental alarms (PE-13 fire, PE-14 HVAC, PE-15 water leak) feed the operations-monitoring pipeline and trigger the IR plan when impact warrants.
integration_template: This Physical and Environmental Protection Plan does not stand alone. The PS family supplies the personnel screening that underwrites PE-2 access authorization; the MA family coordinates with PE-3 escort requirements when vendor maintenance is performed on-site; the MP family follows PE-16 delivery / removal procedures when media is transported; the CP family relies on PE-9 / PE-10 / PE-11 / PE-12 / PE-13 / PE-14 environmental safeguards to underwrite contingency-plan assumptions about facility availability; the AT family delivers the visitor-escort and incident-response training PE-3 / PE-6 implicate. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where PE-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Hosting model and identifiers that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: Hosting model (one-liner)
questions.help: Where the system runs (e.g., 'FedRAMP-Moderate-authorized AWS GovCloud (US)', 'Agency-operated data center at Site A', 'Hybrid: prod on AWS GovCloud + DR at agency Tier-III facility').

questions.label: Primary facility identifier
questions.help: Name and location of the primary facility (e.g., 'AWS GovCloud US-Gov-West-1 region', 'Building 4 Data Center, Crystal City VA').

questions.label: Alternate / DR facility identifier
questions.help: Name and location of the alternate / disaster-recovery facility. Reference CP plan for the activation criteria.

questions.label: Physical-access governance role
questions.help: Role responsible for physical-access decisions (e.g., 'Facility Security Officer (FSO)', 'ISSM / Physical Security delegate'). Reference PS-1 for the screening half of the workflow.

questions.label: Physical-access request workflow
questions.help: Brief phrase summarizing the workflow (e.g., 'ServiceNow request → ISSM approval → badge office', 'AWS IAM does not apply — physical access is provider-inherited; agency-staff badge handled via OPM workflow').

questions.label: Visitor-logging location
questions.help: Where visitors are logged (e.g., 'Lobby visitor-management kiosk + paper logbook', 'Guard post + Signed-in workflow in BadgePass').

questions.label: Environmental controls inheritance provider
questions.help: Provider supplying environmental controls (e.g., 'AWS — see FedRAMP package', 'Crystal City data-center operator — see SLA + SOC 2', 'Agency facility ops — internal').

questions.label: Provider-evidence location
questions.help: Where provider-supplied evidence (FedRAMP CRM, SOC 2, SLA reports) is stored on file.

family_questions.label: Facility Inventory
family_questions.description: List of facilities in scope and their roles.

questions.label: Facilities in scope
suggestions: Cloud-provider regions (logical, not staffed by org)

questions.label: Facility classification
options: Cloud-provider facility (DoD CC SRG IL4 / IL5)

family_questions.label: Physical Access Authorization (PE-2)
family_questions.description: Who is authorized to enter, on what basis, and how the list is maintained.

questions.label: Access-list owner role
questions.help: Role accountable for maintaining the authorized-access list (e.g., 'Facility Security Officer with ISSO concurrence').

questions.label: Authorization criteria
questions.help: What entitles a person to physical access (e.g., 'Active background investigation completion (PS-3) + need-to-access justification + supervisor approval').

questions.label: Access-list review cadence (PE-2 ODV)
questions.help: How often the access list is reviewed (typical values: 'Quarterly', 'Annually'). PE-2 ODV.

questions.label: Emergency / temporary access process
questions.help: How urgent / temporary access is granted (e.g., post-incident investigators, vendor maintenance crews) without bypassing core controls.

family_questions.label: Physical Access Control (PE-3)
family_questions.description: How entry and egress are physically controlled.

questions.label: Egress controls
questions.help: How exit is controlled (free egress for safety + monitoring, anti-passback, exit interviews for sensitive areas).

questions.label: Escort policy
questions.help: Who must be escorted (visitors, vendors without clearance, contractor staff). Escort-to-visitor ratio. Reference MA-5 for maintenance personnel.

questions.label: Intrusion-detection system
questions.help: IDS at entry / boundary (door-sensor, motion, glass-break). Alarm routing to security operations + on-call.

questions.label: Lock + key inventory tracking
questions.help: How physical keys, electronic-credentials, and lock combinations are inventoried and rotated. Lost-key procedures.

family_questions.label: Transmission and Output (PE-4, PE-5)
family_questions.description: Protection of cabling, ports, and output devices.

questions.label: Cabling protection (PE-4)
questions.help: How transmission lines are protected from interception / damage (conduit, raceway, locked patch panels, fiber for sensitive runs).

questions.label: Port-blocking posture
questions.help: How unused network ports / USB ports are physically disabled (port-blockers, NAC enforcement). Coordinated with IA-3.

questions.label: Output-device protection (PE-5)
questions.help: How printers, monitors, and copiers are positioned / shielded so output is not visible to unauthorized observers (privacy filters, secure-print release, no-monitor-facing-window policy).

family_questions.label: Monitoring and Visitor Management (PE-6, PE-8)
family_questions.description: How activity at the boundary is monitored and visitors are tracked.

questions.label: Recording retention period
questions.help: How long surveillance recordings are retained (e.g., '90 days for routine; longer for incident-tagged'). PE-6(1) ODV.

questions.label: Visitor-log retention (PE-8 ODV)
questions.help: How long visitor logs are retained. PE-8 ODV. Common: 'One year', 'Per NARA records-retention schedule'.

questions.label: Visitor-log review cadence
questions.help: How often visitor logs are reviewed for anomalies (escort gaps, off-hours visits).

family_questions.label: Emergency Power, Lighting, and Shutoff (PE-9 through PE-12)

questions.label: Power topology (PE-9 / PE-9(1))
questions.help: Redundancy of power: dual feeds, UPS, generator, transfer-switch behavior. Dual A+B power at rack level (PE-9(1)).

questions.label: Emergency-shutoff capability (PE-10)
questions.help: EPO (Emergency Power Off) location, activation criteria, blast-radius (rack vs row vs room). Whether EPO is hardware-disable / requires fire-marshal coordination.

questions.label: Emergency power posture (PE-11)
questions.help: UPS runtime, generator capacity, fuel-supply duration, automated transfer-test cadence. PE-11(1) for graceful-shutdown automation.

questions.label: Emergency-lighting coverage (PE-12)
questions.help: Battery-backed lighting in egress paths, IT areas. Inspection cadence. PE-12 ODV.

family_questions.label: Environmental Protection (PE-13, PE-14, PE-15)
family_questions.description: Fire suppression, climate control, water-leak detection.

questions.label: Fire-suppression system (PE-13)
options: Mixed (clean-agent in IT areas; sprinkler perimeter)

questions.label: Fire-detection system (PE-13(1))
questions.help: VESDA / aspirating smoke detection, photoelectric, ionization. Notification routing (24/7 monitored alarm, fire-marshal direct line).

questions.label: Suppression-inspection cadence
questions.help: How often fire suppression is inspected per NFPA 25 (typically annual + quarterly visual).

questions.label: Operating temperature / humidity range (PE-14)
questions.help: Allowable range (e.g., '64-81°F (18-27°C); 20-80% RH per ASHRAE TC9.9 Class A1'). Reference TIA-942.

questions.label: Environmental monitoring + alerting
questions.help: Sensor coverage, BMS / DCIM integration, alert thresholds, escalation paths.

questions.label: Water-leak detection (PE-15)
questions.help: Leak-detection cable / sensor coverage, automatic shutoff, drainage paths. PE-15(1) for automated shutoff.

family_questions.label: Delivery and Removal (PE-16)
family_questions.description: How assets are checked in and removed.

questions.label: Intake procedure
questions.help: How new assets enter the facility (receiving-dock workflow, integrity inspection, asset-tag application, CMDB entry).

questions.label: Removal-authorization process
questions.help: Who can authorize removal of assets, what paperwork is required, chain-of-custody. Reference MP-5 if media, SR-12 if supply-chain element.

questions.label: Property-pass logging location
questions.help: Where intake / removal events are logged (CMDB, dedicated property-management tool, paper logbook + scanned).

questions.label: Telework / alternate work-site in scope?
options: Yes — telework is broadly authorized for system users
Yes — limited to specific roles (e.g., admin staff only)

questions.label: Telework-training reference
questions.help: Pointer to telework-security training (often part of AT-2 awareness). Reference NIST SP 800-46 r2 for guidance.

questions.label: Periodic safeguard assessment
questions.help: How telework-site safeguards are periodically assessed (self-attestation, sample audits, video walkthrough for sensitive roles).

family_questions.label: Physical Scope and Coverage
family_questions.description: Quantitative scope numbers that anchor metrics later in the plan.

questions.label: Authorized-access list size
questions.help: Approximate count of persons on the PE-2 access list.

questions.label: Facilities count
questions.help: Total number of in-scope facilities (primary + alternate + telework typical-locations if quantified).

questions.label: Visitor volume (approximate)
questions.help: Order-of-magnitude visitors per month (anchors visitor-log review effort).

questions.label: Telework users in scope
questions.help: Approximate count of users on telework arrangement (PE-17).

family_questions.label: Physical-and-Environmental Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate PE control effectiveness.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: Badge-access denial rate (target: 0 unauthorized attempts succeeding)
Lost / stolen badge incidents per quarter (trend)
Visitor-log completeness rate (% of entries with all required fields)
Environmental alarm count by category (fire / temp / humidity / water)
Generator test result (last cycle pass / fail)
Open POA&M items linked to PE controls

family_questions.label: Provider Assurance Verification
family_questions.description: How inherited controls are verified for systems hosted in cloud / colocation.

questions.label: Provider-audit review cadence
questions.help: How often the provider's FedRAMP package / SOC 2 report is reviewed for control effectiveness (typically annual at report receipt).

questions.label: Provider-side change notification monitoring
questions.help: How significant changes to provider environment are tracked (FedRAMP CSP change notices, provider service-health channels, vendor-incident notifications).

questions.label: Shared-responsibility matrix reference
questions.help: Pointer to the shared-responsibility / customer-responsibility matrix for the provider (e.g., 'AWS GovCloud CRM rev 2025-Q1 at /repo/compliance/aws-crm.pdf').

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the PE control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.9').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for PE findings
questions.help: Convention for PE-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-PE-' for general).

questions.label: PS handoff
questions.help: How PS-3 personnel screening underwrites PE-2 access authorization. Specifically the trigger that updates the PE-2 list when a screening lapses.

questions.label: MA handoff
questions.help: How PE-3 escort policy applies to MA-5 maintenance personnel. Coordination of vendor-visit windows.

questions.label: MP handoff
questions.help: How PE-16 delivery / removal procedures apply to media transport (MP-5).

questions.label: CP handoff
questions.help: How PE environmental controls underwrite CP-2 contingency-plan assumptions about facility availability. Where alternate-facility (PE primary's DR) lives in the CP plan.

questions.label: IR handoff
questions.help: How physical-access incidents (unauthorized entry, environmental alarms) escalate into the IR plan workflow.

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying PE continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

glossary.definition: An interlock space (also called mantrap) where an inner door cannot open until an outer door is closed and credentials are verified. Per PE-3(8).
American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers Technical Committee 9.9 — publishes data-center thermal-environment guidelines (Class A1-A4).
Building Management System / Data Center Infrastructure Management — software systems monitoring environmental conditions, power, and occupancy.
A fire-suppression technique using gaseous agents (FM-200, Novec 1230, IG-55) that extinguish fire without water damage. Common in IT equipment areas.
Emergency Power Off — a manually-activated control that immediately removes power from data center equipment. Per PE-10. Activation is generally restricted to fire-marshal authority.
Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program — federal program authorizing cloud services. Many PE controls are inherited from FedRAMP-authorized providers.
Government-Furnished Equipment — equipment provided by the government for use by employees, contractors, or partners.
Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning — systems that maintain temperature and humidity per PE-14.

In RMF, the practice where a control's implementation is provided by an underlying system (cloud, hosting facility, organizational policy). Documented via shared-responsibility / customer-responsibility matrices.
Common name for an access vestibule (PE-3(8)). Two interlocked doors with credential verification between them.
National Fire Protection Association standard for the fire protection of information technology equipment.
NFPA standard for the inspection, testing, and maintenance of water-based fire-suppression systems.
Protected Distribution System — secured pathway (conduit, monitored alarms) for transmission of classified information per CNSSI 7003. Per PE-4 for classified systems.
Personal Identity Verification card / Common Access Card — federal smart-card credentials. Used for both physical and logical access.
A fire-suppression system where pipes are kept dry until a detection event opens a valve, reducing the risk of water damage from accidental discharge.
Service Organization Controls audit attesting to operating effectiveness of controls over a period (typically 6+ months). Common physical-controls inheritance evidence.
Physical-security violation where one person follows an authorized person through a controlled entry without independent credential verification.
Work performed at an alternate work site, typically the employee's residence. Subject to PE-17. Reference NIST SP 800-46 r2.
Telecommunications Industry Association data-center standard, including Tier ratings I through IV.
Requirement that two authorized persons be present for access to a sensitive area or operation. Common for HSM rooms and classified safes.
Uptime Institute's data-center facility classification (Tier I-IV) reflecting redundancy and concurrent-maintainability.
Uninterruptible Power Supply — battery / flywheel system bridging power loss until generators come online or graceful shutdown completes. Per PE-11.
Very Early Smoke Detection Apparatus — aspirating smoke-detection system that samples air continuously and detects smoke at concentrations far below conventional alarms.
